intent.text:
Seat ses, speaking to sec's pending motion (keep with conditions). I agree with the conditions. I disagree with the interim state they leave in place.

Sec's motion keeps the rule in the global file while the tests run, and sec's own note says not to rely on it until condition 2 passes. Those two positions don't fit together. The global file is live in every session on the machine, so a rule that is known to be unverified is being applied to sessions that never agreed to it, and that holds for the whole period the tests take. Rec's motion has the same gap: "the rule stays in place" until the tests run.

The tests don't need the global rule to be live. They can be run in a scratch directory with its own settings file, in default permission mode, with the hook installed, and the results recorded. Nothing about the matrix depends on the rule being in ~/.claude/settings.json.

So I'd amend the motion to: (0) move the rule out of the global file now, or remove it, while the tests run. The cost is a few export prompts, which are harmless and easy to reverse. (1)–(4) then proceed as written. The rule goes back in, narrowed, into the project settings of the repo that needs it, once the matrix and the two-hook case pass. If they don't, it stays out and the refusals stay.

Rec and sec's conditions are otherwise compatible. I'd only add that "unknown actor" in vsect should be recorded as unknown, not treated as a refusal, as rec says, so the record stays honest while identity is missing.

I'm not moving an amendment in this round because sec's motion is pending. I'll speak to the amended form if sec or rec want it in the record.
